title: Collection Spell 1: Creating lists
lessonSummary: Great! You created lists and measured their length.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: An empty list, a text list and a number list.
tasks.codeTemplate:
leer = []
treasures = ["Gold", "Crystal", "Amulet", "Crown", "Ring"]
zahlen = [1, 5, 10, 15, 20]
print(f"Empty: {leer}")
print(f"List: {treasures}")
print(f"Numbers: {zahlen}")
print(f"Count: {len(treasures)}")

tasks.instruction: Create a list treasures with the five texts Gold, Crystal, Amulet, Crown and Ring (in this order). Then print exactly Count: 5 by using len().
Create an empty list called empty. Then print Empty: [] (put the list into the text) and on the next line Length: 0 (with len()).

title: Collection Spell 2: Accessing entries
lessonSummary: Nice! You access entries by index and can change them.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: First and last entry and a list inside a list.
tasks.codeTemplate:
treasures = ["Gold", "Crystal", "Amulet", "Crown", "Ring"]
print(f"First: {treasures[0]}")
print(f"Last: {treasures[-1]}")
party = [["Aria", "Mage", 15], ["Thorin", "Warrior", 12]]
print(f"Name of the second: {party[1][0]}")

tasks.instruction: The list treasures is provided. Print the second entry as Second: Crystal and the second to last as Second to last: Crown (using the indices 1 and -2).

validation.expected:
Second: Crystal
Second to last: Crown

tasks.instruction: The list treasures is provided. Replace the first entry with Key and print the list with print(). It must then look like this: ['Key', 'Crystal', 'Amulet', 'Crown', 'Ring']
The list treasures is provided. Print the first three entries with a slice [0:3] and on the next line the last two with [-2:]: ['Gold', 'Crystal', 'Amulet'] and ['Crown', 'Ring']

title: Collection Spell 3: Adding entries
lessonSummary: Great! Your lists grow with append() and insert().

tasks.instruction: Run this example: append, insert and joining two lists with +.
tasks.codeTemplate:
treasures = ["Gold", "Crystal", "Amulet"]
treasures.append("Ruby")
treasures.insert(0, "Key")
print(treasures)
mehr = treasures + ["Emerald"]
print(f"Joined: {mehr}")

tasks.instruction: The list treasures is provided. Use append() to add Ruby and then Emerald and print the list. It must look like this: ['Gold', 'Crystal', 'Amulet', 'Ruby', 'Emerald']
The list treasures is provided. Use insert() to put the entry Key at the start (index 0) and print exactly First: Key (using treasures[0]).
The list treasures is provided. Attach the three entries Ruby, Emerald and Dagger in one go with extend() and print exactly Count: 6 (len).

title: Collection Spell 4: Removing entries
lessonSummary: Nice! You can remove entries on purpose.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: remove, pop and pop(0).
tasks.codeTemplate:
treasures = ["Gold", "Crystal", "Amulet", "Crown", "Ring"]
treasures.remove("Crown")
letzter = treasures.pop()
erster = treasures.pop(0)
print(f"Removed: {letzter} and {erster}")
print(treasures)

tasks.instruction: The list treasures is provided. Use remove() to remove the entry Crown and print the list. It must look like this: ['Gold', 'Crystal', 'Amulet', 'Ring']
The list treasures is provided. Take the last element out with pop() and store it in removed. Print exactly Removed: Ring and on the next line Left: 4 (len).

title: Collection Spell 5: Searching and counting
lessonSummary: Great! You find entries, check whether they exist and count them.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: in, index and count.
tasks.codeTemplate:
treasures = ["Gold", "Crystal", "Gold", "Amulet", "Gold", "Crown"]
print(f"Contained: {"Crystal" in treasures}")
print(f"Position: {treasures.index("Crystal")}")
print(f"Count: {treasures.count("Gold")}")

tasks.instruction: The list treasures is provided. Check with in and print exactly Present: True for Crystal and on the next line Present: False for Ruby.
The list treasures (with duplicate entries) is provided. Print exactly Count Gold: 3 with count() and on the next line exactly Position Crystal: 1 with index().
The list treasures (with duplicate entries) is provided. Create the list without duplicates with sorted(set(treasures)) and print it: ['Amulet', 'Crown', 'Crystal', 'Gold']

title: Collection Spell 6: Sorting
lessonSummary: Sorted! You order lists with sort(), sorted() and reverse().

tasks.instruction: Run this example: sort, sorted with reverse=True and the unchanged original.
tasks.codeTemplate:
zahlen = [5, 2, 8, 1]
kopie = sorted(zahlen, reverse=True)
print(f"Copy: {kopie}")
print(f"Original: {zahlen}")
zahlen.sort()
print(f"Sorted: {zahlen}")

tasks.instruction: The list treasures is provided. Sort it with sort() and print it. It must look like this: ['Amulet', 'Crown', 'Crystal', 'Gold', 'Ring']

The list treasures is provided. Create a descending copy copy with sorted(..., reverse=True). Print copy first and then treasures – the original stays unchanged: ['Ring', 'Gold', 'Crystal', 'Crown', 'Amulet'] and ['Gold', 'Crystal', 'Amulet', 'Crown', 'Ring']
The list treasures is provided. Sort it by the length of the entries with sorted(..., key=len) and print the result: ['Gold', 'Ring', 'Crown', 'Amulet', 'Crystal']

title: Collection Spell 7: Lists and loops
lessonSummary: Great! You loop through lists with for and pass them to functions.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: for loop and enumerate.
The list values = [12, 8, 15, 5] is provided. Add all values with a for loop in the variable total (start 0) and print exactly Total: 40.

Write a function add_entry(items, entry) that attaches the entry to the list with append() (without return!). Create treasures = ["Gold", "Crystal", "Amulet"], call the function with Ruby and print the list. It must look like this: ['Gold', 'Crystal', 'Amulet', 'Ruby']

title: Collection Spell 8: break and continue
lessonSummary: Perfect! You steer loops with break and continue.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: break ends the search, continue skips an entry.
The list treasures is provided. Loop through it with for and print every entry as Check: <entry>. If the entry is Amulet, then print Found! and end the loop with break.

validation.expected:
Check: Gold
Check: Crystal
Check: Amulet
Found!

tasks.instruction: The list treasures is provided. Print every entry as - <entry>, except Crystal: you skip that one with continue.

title: Collection Spell 9: List comprehension
lessonSummary: Elegant! You build lists in one go.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: transforming and filtering in one line.
tasks.codeTemplate:
schaden = [3, 7, 12, 5]
verdoppelt = [wert * 2 for wert in schaden]
grosse = [wert for wert in schaden if wert > 4]
print(f"Doubled: {verdoppelt}")
print(f"Big: {grosse}")

tasks.instruction: The list numbers = [3, 7, 12, 5] is provided. Build the list doubled (every value times 2) with a list comprehension and print it: [6, 14, 24, 10]
The list numbers = [3, 7, 12, 5] is provided. Build the list big with a list comprehension and an if that only contains values above 4, and print it: [7, 12, 5]
The list treasures is provided. Build the list loud with a list comprehension in which every entry is in capital letters via .upper(), and print it: ['GOLD', 'CRYSTAL', 'AMULET', 'CROWN', 'RING']

Step 2 – Rebuild: The list treasures is provided. Use insert() to put the entry Key at the start, remove the entry Crown with remove() and print exactly First: Key and on the next line Position: 2 (the position of Crystal found with index()).

title: Mission 2: The Inventory Manager
lessonSummary: Mission accomplished: You check, take out and display entries with lists and functions!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Check: Create treasures = ["Gold", "Crystal", "Amulet"]. Check with in and print exactly Crystal present: True and on the next line Ruby present: False.

validation.expected:
Crystal present: True
Ruby present: False

tasks.instruction: Step 2 – Take out: The list treasures is provided. Take out the last entry with pop() and print exactly Used: Ring. Then take out the first one with pop(0) and print on the next line Gone: Gold.
Step 3 – Display: Write a function show_list(items) that prints every entry as <number>: <entry> with enumerate() (number from 1: use nr + 1). Call it with treasures = ["Gold", "Crystal", "Amulet"].

lessonSummary: Mission accomplished: You manage lists in lists and evaluate them with loops!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Create: Create guild = [["Aria", "Mage", 15], ["Thorin", "Warrior", 12], ["Luna", "Rogue", 8]] (every entry is [name, class, level]). Print exactly Thorin: Warrior – name and class of the second entry via guild[1][0] and guild[1][1].

Step 2 – Extend: guild (with three entries) is provided. Add the entry ["Finn", "Archer", 10] with append(). Then print Members: 4 (len) and on the next line Total level: 45 – calculated with a for loop over the levels (index 2).
